identity_proofing.method: OpenID Connect for Identity Assurance verified_claims, recorded by a recognized identity verifier; each ID can show the trust framework and assurance level
identity_proofing.sybil_resistance: one principal record per verified identity: a legal entity by LEI or registration number, a person by name, jurisdiction and date of birth
identity_proofing.reverification: a verification expires; while it is lapsed the principal cannot register agents and its agents are suspended

authentication.principals: an Ed25519 key enrolled with the principal record; every request is signed (RFC 9421)
authentication.agents: an Ed25519 key whose possession the agent proves at registration; a separate key per counterparty or per presentation is bound into each ID

modes.pairwise: reusable: at most one per agent and counterparty (a PPID)

ids.claims: every claim except the ID is selectively disclosable by the agent

by: a delegating agent, for its sub-agents
this directory, for fraud or under its operating rules
a recognized authority, by legal order
revocation.status: a published Token Status List, fetched whole: this directory does not learn which ID a counterparty checks

held: pairwise IDs issued and their counterparties
not_held: a lasting link from a single-use ID to its agent (the ID carries a sealed reference only this directory can open)
records.log: every change is an entry in an append-only Merkle log with signed tree heads

disclosure.to_counterparties: identity claims only where the principal's disclosure policy names the claim and the counterparty

attribution.process: a legal order from a recognized authority that names the ID; single-use IDs also need the sealed reference the counterparty kept
attribution.principal_notified: yes, unless the order forbids it

disclosure.incidents: reports are relayed to the principal without telling the reporter who the principal is

practices.signing_keys: held in files on the operator's server; no hardware protection and no rotation (reference implementation)
practices.security: a reference implementation for discussion and pilots; not operated to a production standard
